label: first copy step (re-reading orig token 0 after <DEL>), longer sequences
explanation: Fires almost only in the copy phase (99% of mass), and mostly on the step right after <DEL>: the input there is the first original token fed back and the output is original token 1 (recall_idx==1 holds 91% of mass, 51% firing rate). How often it fires there grows with sequence length: rate is about 0.5% at L=4 and rises toward t=10 for L=9. It is weakly active at recall_idx 2 (8% of mass) and at the delimiter step (1%). It never fires during the original phase. Magnitude also depends on the first token: 0, x, c and f give the largest activations, and top examples start with c, x or 0. Restricting to L>=6 trades recall for precision (dev P 0.72, R 0.74, mass recall 0.89). Many recall_idx==1 steps in mid-length sequences stay inactive, and the first-token dependence is not captured.
